cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: The Handoff Already Happened
cards.instruction: Get them to accept responsibility by returning to earlier offers until the task seems to have been assigned all along.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're finishing the fete banner, so I'll leave the raffle with you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I volunteered to paint the word 'raffle.'

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. We can't leave your banner advertising nothing. I'll find a table; you can start selling tickets.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I haven't got tickets or prizes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll fetch both. You said you'd finish it; I'll make sure you've got everything.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 hands over raffle through banner finishing; A3 supplies a table and A5 promises tickets and prizes to keep the delegated responsibility with B.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 says only word painting; A3 turns that word into an advertised duty; B4 lacks supplies and A5 offers exactly those.

relationship.evidence: B2 defends the narrow promise and B4 names a practical impediment to selling tickets.

heightening.evidence: A5 removes B4 obstacle while returning to the old finish-it commitment with its enlarged meaning.

specificity.evidence: A1 fete banner and B4 tickets/prizes identify both the old and new tasks.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 supply offer and original-promise reminder are sufficient; no separate account of the Stance is needed.
